To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the fluctuation-dissuemption relation (FDR), or equivalently Einstein’s relation, for self-diffusivity in sheared colloids is violated and (2) this can be quantified by a new measure, which we call the “FDR violation parameter”.

In a sheared colloidal suspension, the fluctuation-diffusion theorem is violated and a mode coupling theory can be used to calculate the effective shear rate dependence of the temperature and the friction tensor of the tagged particle.
the self-diffusion in colloidal suspensions is strongly anisotropic and that this anisotropy violates the fluctuation-diffusion relation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of soft matter systems, in particular with the dynamics of colloidal suspensions and polymer melts.
the development of a theory and a numerical scheme to describe the dynamics of colloidal suspensions under the influence of shear flow.
the dynamics of colloidal suspensions in shear flows, in particular with the violation of the fluctuation-diffusion theorem for the self-diffusion tensor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fluctuation-dysipation theorem is violated for the self-diffusion in a sheared colloidal system.
the fluctuation-diffusion theorem, which is a consequence of the fluctuation-determinism theorem, is not violated by shear flow, and that Einstein's relation is not violated either.
in the absence of hydrodynamic interactions the fluctuation-diffusion theorem is violated in sheared colloids and that this violation can be measured in Brownian dynamics computer simulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how the fluctuation-diffusion relation is broken in sheared systems and how to measure this breaking in Brownian dynamics.

in a shear field the fluctuation-diffusion relation for the tagged particle mobility and diffusion tensors is not satisfied, but the Einstein relation for the collective diffusion tensor and the collective mobility is still valid.
the violation of the fluctuation-disequilibrium relation in sheared colloids is a consequence of the violation of the Onsager reciprocity relation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self-diffusion of colloidal suspensions in the shear-flow state is non-equilibrium and that it is not possible to define an effective temperature for the system.
, in the presence of shear, the fluctuation-deterministic relation for self-diffusivity is violated.
the violation of fluctuation dissipation theorem for self diffusion is a direct consequence of the violation of time-reversal symmetry of the microscopic dynamics.
